chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-ʿAṭṭār, from his father, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"For me to perform the ẓuhr salat (prayer) in the time of the ʿaṣr salat (prayer) is more beloved to me than to perform it before the sun declines; for if I perform it before the sun declines, it is not counted for me, and if I perform it in the time of the ʿaṣr salat (prayer), it is counted for me."

key_terms.الظُّهْرَ: the ẓuhr salat (prayer), the noon prayer
key_terms.تَزُولَ الشَّمْسُ: the sun declines from its zenith, marking the beginning of ẓuhr time
key_terms.حُسِبَتْ لِي: it is counted for me, meaning it is considered valid and accepted
key_terms.لَمْ تُحْتَسَبْ لِي: it is not counted for me, meaning it is not considered valid
key_terms.وَقْتِ الْعَصْرِ: the time of the ʿaṣr salat (prayer), indicating a later valid period

ai.seo_question: Is the ẓuhr salat (prayer) valid if performed before zawāl, and is delaying it better than praying too early?
ai.summary: This hadith states that performing the ẓuhr salat (prayer) after its proper time has begun—even if delayed until the time associated with ʿaṣr—is preferable to performing it before the sun’s decline. It emphasizes that a prayer offered before its legislated time is not valid or counted, while one performed within valid time is accepted.
